title: Mechanical Assembly Line Controller
description: The user operates a steampunk assembly line where interlocking gears drive a conveyor system that animates boxes. Players must configure gear rotation speed, direction, and torque through a control panel, then trigger the box animation sequence at precise timing intervals to successfully package and dispatch crates along the belt.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load 'shared_assets/gears.glb' and 'shared_assets/BoxAnimated.glb'. Scene setup: Place the gears model at the left side of the scene as the mechanical driver. Clone the BoxAnimated model 3 times and position them spaced along an imaginary conveyor line extending to the right. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at the origin. Add ambient light intensity 0.5, a directional light from (5, 10, 7) with intensity 1.2, and a warm point light near the gears with orange tint. Create an HTML overlay control panel with: (1) a speed slider (0.1 to 3.0) controlling gear rotation speed, (2) a direction toggle button switching gear rotation between clockwise and counter-clockwise, (3) a torque dropdown with Low/Medium/High options that scales gear model size between 0.8x, 1.0x, and 1.2x, (4) a 'Start Belt' button that begins translating boxes slowly from left to right across the scene at a rate proportional to gear speed, (5) an 'Animate Box' button that plays the BoxAnimated GLB animation clip on the box nearest to a marked dispatch zone on the right side using THREE.AnimationMixer, (6) a 'Dispatch' button that fades out the animated box and respawns it at the start position. Validate all parameters: speed slider must be set above 0.5, direction must be toggled at least once, and torque must be set to Medium or High before the Start Belt button becomes enabled. The Animate Box button only activates when a box enters the dispatch zone. The Dispatch button only works after the box animation completes. Track and display a counter showing successfully dispatched boxes. Gears must visually rotate continuously once the belt starts, with rotation speed and direction matching the controls. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop. Enable OrbitControls for camera interaction.
